summary: High CPU utilization and ALB 5xx errors on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890
root_cause: The Nginx reverse-proxy service on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 stopped responding after an OOM kill at 10:37 UTC, causing the attached ALB target group to mark the instance unhealthy and return HTTP 502/504 to clients.
evidence: CloudWatch: CPUUtilization on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 sustained above 96% for 8 consecutive minutes (10:29–10:37 UTC).
CloudTrail: no configuration or deployment API calls recorded on this instance in the preceding 24 hours, ruling out a recent change.
ALB access logs: target_status_code 502/504 for 214 requests routed to i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 between 10:37–10:45 UTC.
System log (via CloudWatch Logs agent): 'Out of memory: Killed process 1842 (nginx)' recorded at 10:37:03 UTC.
recommendations: Restart the Nginx service on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 and confirm target group health returns to healthy.
Increase the instance type or add a swap volume to absorb short memory spikes.
Add a CloudWatch alarm on MemoryUtilization (via CWAgent) with a threshold below the OOM-kill point.
Review the Auto Scaling group's health-check grace period so a single OOM event triggers replacement sooner.

summary: Memory utilization high across Auto Scaling group
root_cause: A gradual memory leak in the application process caused average MemoryUtilization across the Auto Scaling group to climb from 54% to 82% over 6 hours, with no corresponding traffic increase.
evidence: CloudWatch: group-average MemoryUtilization trending upward linearly since 04:00 UTC.
No scale-out events triggered because the configured scaling policy tracks CPU, not memory.
recommendations: Add a memory-based scaling policy or scheduled restart to mitigate the leak short-term.
File an engineering ticket to profile and fix the underlying memory leak.

summary: Disk space running low on db-prod-instance
root_cause: Free storage space on db-prod-instance dropped below the 20% warning threshold due to unbounded growth of the slow query log.
evidence: CloudWatch: FreeStorageSpace on db-prod-instance at 18.4% of allocated capacity.
CloudTrail: no recent storage-modifying API calls; growth attributed to log accumulation.
recommendations: Rotate or disable the slow query log, or increase allocated storage.
Enable storage autoscaling on the RDS instance to prevent recurrence.
